name: ganconer

attributes.attribute: male form of the fairy lover or mistress
a Scottish and Irish folkloric figure

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The ganconer belongs to the folk traditions of Scotland and Ireland. The name means the love-talker. Other names are gean-cannah, gan-ceann, and gean-canach. Scottish maidens were told to avoid lonely country roads, especially in the mountains. They might meet a handsome fairy there. A clay pipe marked him. He made promises so sweet that the girl pined away after he vanished. The ganconer was the male form of the fairy lover. In Ireland the same being was the geancanach. It favored milkmaids. The Irish poet Ethna Carbery wrote of the Love-Talker. She said that whoever meets the Love-Talker must weave her shroud soon. The word also described boastful human men.

okr.objective: Describe the ganconer as the male fairy lover of Scottish and Irish folklore.
key_results: The ganconer lured maidens with sweet promises and a clay pipe.
In Ireland the same being was the geancanach, which favored milkmaids.
Ethna Carbery wrote of the destructive love of the Love-Talker.
The term also applied to boastful human men.
